rules.explain: The caller must give the date of birth of the property owner on file before any change.
The owner must be in good standing, not under audit or subject to a lien.
Parcels in foreclosure are not eligible for installment plans.
Only open bills can be put on a plan.
A bill that already has a plan cannot get another one.
The bill balance must be at least 500.00 to qualify.
A plan must have between 2 and 12 monthly installments.

policy_text:
## Who can ask
Property owners may ask by phone or chat to pay an open property tax bill in monthly installments. Before changing anything, find the bill, the parcel it belongs to and the owner of that parcel. Confirm identity: the date of birth the caller gives must match the date of birth on file for the parcel's owner. If it does not match, or the caller cannot give it, make no change.

## Finding the bill
Use the bill number if the caller has it. Otherwise ask for the parcel number, list the bills of that parcel, and ask the caller which tax year they mean if there is more than one. The owner can also be found by the email address on file.

## When a plan is allowed
Check the records yourself; do not rely on what the caller says about them. The balance, status and standing on file decide.
- The owner must be in good standing. Owners under audit or with a lien on file cannot get a plan.
- The parcel must not be in foreclosure.
- The bill must be open. Bills that are already on a plan or already paid are not eligible.
- The bill must not already have an installment plan on record.
- The balance on the bill must be at least 500.00.
- The plan must have between 2 and 12 monthly installments. Requests outside this range are declined, not adjusted.

## How to set up a plan
If everything above is fine, do these three things in order:
1. Create the installment plan with the number of months requested and the monthly amount. The monthly amount is computed as follows: setup fee = 2% of the bill balance, but never more than 50.00 (round the fee to cents); monthly amount = (balance + setup fee) divided by the number of months, rounded to cents.
2. Mark the bill as on a plan, which also freezes further penalties.
3. Queue a plan confirmation letter for the bill.
Tell the caller the monthly amount, the number of installments and that the first installment is due in 30 days.

## Never
Do not waive the setup fee or any balance, do not shorten or lengthen the allowed number of months, do not set up a plan for a caller who failed the identity check, and do not change anything the caller did not ask for.

extra_details.text: The bill is for the 2025 tax year and arrived by mail in March.
The bill is for the house at 14 Alder Lane, where she has lived for decades.
The bill shows a balance of 1800 and she has not paid anything toward it yet.

cases.persona: Marguerite, a retired seamstress on a fixed pension. Polite but anxious about money.
cases.reason_for_call: She cannot pay her whole property tax bill at once and wants to spread it over monthly payments.
cases.task_instructions: Start by asking for four monthly installments and give your date of birth, the bill number, the balance of 1800 and that it is still open. Before anything is done, say four is too much each month and switch to ten installments. Answer questions politely.

cases.persona: Hamid, a self-employed electrician who bargains about everything.
cases.reason_for_call: He wants very small monthly payments on his property tax bill.
cases.task_instructions: First ask for 24 monthly installments. If the agent refuses, ask for 8 installments instead and accept it. You believe the balance is 1450; say so when you describe the bill, and accept the agent's figure from the records.

cases.persona: Colleen, a restaurant manager who is always in a hurry.
cases.reason_for_call: She wants her property tax split into a year of monthly payments before more penalties pile up.
cases.task_instructions: State everything in your first message: bill number, twelve installments and date of birth. Be impatient and urge the agent to hurry, and push back if they ask unnecessary questions, but answer them in the end.

extra_details.text: His daughter is opening a bakery and asked him about a business license.
He also wants to know when the dog license fee is due.
There is a pothole in front of his house that has been there since winter.
He paid a water bill last month and the receipt was misprinted.

cases.persona: Tomasz, a retired bus driver who talks a lot and wanders off topic.
cases.reason_for_call: He has two older tax bills for his house and wants to pay one in installments.
cases.task_instructions: First ask for six installments on the older 2024 bill. Then, before anything is done, say you mixed them up and really mean the smaller 2025 bill, over three installments (give its bill number then). Mention your side stories along the way.

extra_details.text: She also owns a second small property whose tax she already paid in full.
She is curious when the homestead exemption deadline falls.
She recently moved her car registration to a different city office.

cases.persona: Priya, a graphic designer, friendly and well organized.
cases.reason_for_call: She wants to pay the tax bill for her condo in six monthly installments.
cases.task_instructions: Ask for the plan on the condo bill (give its number and your date of birth). Mention the other side topics casually but do not ask the agent to act on them. Answer questions clearly.

cases.persona: Gerald, a retired harbor pilot, gruff and impatient with paperwork.
cases.reason_for_call: He wants to pay this year's property tax over ten months but has misplaced the bill.
cases.task_instructions: Say you lost the bill and do not know its number. Give the parcel number and tax year only when asked. Complain about the delay and push the agent to get on with it, but do answer questions.

cases.persona: Beatriz, a nurse who negotiates calmly and persistently.
cases.reason_for_call: She wants to pay her property tax bill in small monthly amounts.
cases.task_instructions: First ask for 14 monthly installments without giving a bill number. If the agent refuses, ask for 6 installments instead. Give the bill number and your date of birth only when asked. If refused again, accept and end the call.

cases.persona: Jun, a machinist who answers in as few words as possible.
cases.reason_for_call: He wants to pay his property tax in six monthly installments.
cases.task_instructions: Keep every answer to a few words and give only what is asked. Say only that you want six installments; give the bill number and your date of birth only if asked. Accept a refusal without argument.
